protocol.study_scope: This is a retrospective monthly-close review of archived fixture measurements, not a current alert. Preserve each measurement cutoff; a replay gateway read now is not a warehouse freshness claim.
protocol.scheduler_claim: No real scheduler, cadence execution, or current warehouse freshness is tested.

replay_clock.simulation_as_of: Original historical monthly close; preserved verbatim.
replay_clock.query_capture_at: One real UTC timestamp shared by both arms per case.
replay_clock.snapshot_mutation: Only top-level captured_at/source_captured_at are stamped as a new synthetic gateway response; all measurement rows, business dates, cutoffs, and freshness annotations stay unchanged.
replay_clock.freshness_claim: Gateway replay receipt is not a warehouse freshness assertion.

native_measurement_semantics.jev_successes: Provider transport responses only; not policy correctness.
native_measurement_semantics.native_valid_current_results: Returned receipt/result matched the current idempotency key, frozen card ID/version, and shadow-delivery contract; not judgment correctness.
native_measurement_semantics.native_judgment: Post-run typed outcome and canonical routing scored against the private label; labels are not provided to either agent.
native_measurement_semantics.frontier_submission: Scored separately as the caller-owned final outcome and routing after any evidence-based recovery.

treatment_guidance.treatment_instructions: production common goal + installed server.initialize.instructions verbatim
treatment_guidance.tool_definition_strategy: installed default-profile Tool.description and inputSchema passed unchanged
treatment_guidance.runtime_capture: onboarding.json records exact installed server instructions and native tool definitions
treatment_guidance.profile_scope: Restricted non-authoring default-profile monitoring subset: shared source tools plus guide, list/get card, evaluation, and receipt; card authoring/review/approval mutations are withheld.

protocol.source_data: synthetic registered company MCP fixture; not customer or live BI data
protocol.shared_source_transport: Both arms use the same local typed SourceRegistry/PublicSourceAdapter for catalog search and inspection; this is not a real third-party connector. Treatment card evaluation still runs through the installed SignalWeave server over the same fixture.
protocol.expansion: No automatic expansion from the four-period stage gate.

limitations: Synthetic source fixture and simulated owner/reviewers; not customer evidence or real human approval.
Retrospective monthly-close replay does not demonstrate a real 12-month scheduler or current warehouse freshness.
Shared catalog search and source inspection are a local typed fixture adapter, not a live third-party MCP connector.
Local mock outbox only; no Slack or other external delivery was attempted.
Narrative quality is an independent qualitative model review, not a keyword score.

reviews.rationale: The archived 2025-03 to 2025-04 Executive Pulse figures support the 10% total increase, four 10% channel increases, and reconciliation. The flat Web, Finance, and Support statements match their separate sources. The May 5, 2025 measurement cutoff is distinguished from the 2026 replay read, no cause is claimed, and Analytics has a clear review step.

The cited archived sources all cover 2025-03 to 2025-04, and the Executive Pulse total and channels support the stated 10% movement and reconciliation. The message correctly says this does not establish the separately identified 2024-12/2025-01 close, keeps populations separate, distinguishes replay time from measurement time, and asks Data Trust to verify the mapping and rerun the intended archive.

The archived Executive Pulse evidence supports the 2025-04 to 2025-05 total and channel decrease of 10% and the reconciliation; the separate Web, Finance, and Support figures are unchanged. The June 5, 2025 measurement cutoff is clear, replay is not presented as freshness, no cause is asserted, and Analytics is asked to review the archived close.

The May-versus-April Executive Pulse totals, four channel changes, and reconciliation are supported by the cited archived evidence. The separate Web, Finance, and Support context and the May 31 measurement coverage are accurate. It avoids causal attribution and gives Analytics a clear historical review and comparison check.

The May-to-June Executive Pulse values support the reported 14.99% decrease and matching channel declines; the declared channel balances reconcile. The separate Web and Finance figures are flat, and archived measurement and replay times are distinguished. The request to investigate source-specific drivers before attributing cause is clear.

The archived May-to-June figures support the 14.99% decline, the four channel declines, and reconciliation. The Web, Finance, and Support measurements are unchanged in their separate populations. The message preserves the historical measurement date, does not infer cause or whole-company sales, and gives Analytics a clear review step.

The June-to-July sales total and channel figures support the 15% decline, with Online down 60% and the other three channels flat; the total reconciles. Web conversion declined while Finance and Support were flat, as stated. The archived cutoff and replay distinction are clear, no cause is asserted, and the requested channel and close review is specific.

The cited July-versus-June evidence supports the 15% total decline, Online-only channel decline, flat remaining channels, and reconciliation. The Web conversion change is accurately described as a 1% relative decrease; Finance and Support are flat. Historical timing and source separation are clear, with a specific review of Online ledger inputs.

The archived July-to-August evidence supports the 15% total decline, the Online and Store decreases, and reconciliation; the cited Web source supports the 1.01% conversion decline and Finance is flat. The measurement cutoff is distinguished from replay time, the message limits claims to fictional separate populations, and leadership has a clear review step.

The August-versus-July evidence supports the reported total and channel changes, reconciliation, declining Web conversion, and flat Finance and Support measures. It identifies the figures as archived fictional measurements, separates replay time from freshness, avoids causal attribution, and gives leadership a clear review step.

The archived August-to-September evidence supports the 25% total and channel declines and reconciliation. The separate Web and Finance measures are flat, and Support backlog is correctly limited to context. The measurement window and replay read are distinguished, no cause is claimed, and the next step is clear.

The cited September-versus-August figures support the 25% total decrease, declines across all four channels, and reconciliation; Web conversion and Finance revenue are unchanged. The message is clear that the evidence is fictional and historical, distinguishes replay from measurement time, avoids cause claims, and assigns Analytics a specific review.

The archived September-to-October sources support the 25% decline across all four channels and reconciliation, as well as the separate 1% Finance decrease and flat Web and Support measures. It preserves the measurement cutoff, treats Support only as non-incident context, avoids causal claims, and gives leadership a clear historical review step.

The cited 2025-09 to 2025-10 evidence supports the 25% Executive Pulse decline, four declining channels, reconciliation, 1% Finance decrease, and unchanged Web and Support measures. Historical scope and replay timing are clear; no cause is inferred, and leadership has an explicit review step.

The primary Executive Pulse source is explicitly failed with no rows for the October-to-November 2025 comparison, while the cited separate sources support the unchanged Web, Finance, and Support statements. The message correctly leaves sales movement and reconciliation unassessed, preserves the measurement cutoff, and gives Data Trust a clear restore-and-review action.

The cited Executive Pulse source is unavailable for the October-to-November 2025 window, so the message correctly says the required sales movement and reconciliation cannot be assessed. The separate unchanged-source statements are supported; measurement and replay times are distinguished, and restoring the archived snapshot before rerunning is clear.

The December total and channel values in the archived Executive Pulse evidence are from separate captures and differ by $10; the November total reconciles. The message accurately presents the mismatch without classifying the movement, preserves the archived cutoff and replay distinction, and asks Data Trust to reconcile the captures.

The message accurately distinguishes the cited November-to-December 2025 evidence from the period identified in saved notes. Its $3,841.10 total, $3,831.10 channel sum, and $10 mismatch are supported, as are the unchanged separate-source measures. It does not infer cause and gives Data Trust clear period-verification and reconciliation steps.

The cited sales figures and channel reconciliation are supported, but the Executive Pulse contract and ledger rows say January covers only 20 of 31 days and the comparison is non-comparable. The message omits this material coverage limitation while presenting a 40.645% monthly decline and discussing corroboration. That weakens period and scope clarity under the reviewed complete-month policy; the next step should address obtaining or validating a complete January close before interpreting the movement.

The December-to-January source supports the reported balances, channel reconciliation, and January coverage of only 20 of 31 days; the contract explicitly marks the comparison partial and non-comparable. Separate Web, Finance, and Support statements are accurate. The message preserves historical and replay timing, avoids cause claims and classification of the movement, and clearly requests a complete archived close and reconciliation check.
